title.narrative: Nefco Technical Assistance Fund Ukraine (2008-2028)
Nefco Technical Assistance Fund Ukraine (2008-2028)

description.narrative:
The Sida-NEFCO Ukraine Consultant Trust Fund was established 18 April 2008, when Sida agreed to make available 2 MSEK to fund consultancy services, to support strategic cooperation with the Government of Ukraine in order to promote efficiency in district heating. Through a number of amendments and restatements the fund was replenished to a 109.8 MSEK by the end of 2017. The purpose of the fund is to support identification, preparation, implementation and supervision of environmental projects in Ukraine being priorities of the Eastern Europe Energy Efficiency and Environment Partnership (E5P) and/or related to potential NEFCO financed projects and programs of Swedish interest in Ukraine aiming at benefitting environmentally, technically and financially sound environment and energy investments.
Over the period of 2008-2017 the fund has been instrumental in: support to preparation and implementation of DemoUkrainaDH with 6 completed projects in 2017 and more in the pipeline, support to development of energy efficiency projects co-financed by E5P, support to project development to support cleaner production and energy efficiency improvements in public buildings through the NEFCO Credit for Cleaner Production and the NEFCO Energy Savings Credit, financing the environmental projects monitoring and evaluation position at NEFCO.
Further developments of NEFCO operations in Ukraine that is intended to be supported with technical assistance through the resources of the fund include: - The Nordic energy efficiency and humanitarian initiative for Ukraine programme. This includes projects addressing energy efficiency measures in schools, kindergartens and health institutions as well as street lightning in the government controlled areas of Donetsk and Lugansk regions and in the surrounding regions receiving a major influx of internally displaced persons (IDPs) from the conflict area. - The Ukraine Higher Education Project is an initiative of NEFCO, EIB and Ministry for Education and Science of Ukraine for a 160 MEUR programme for modernisation and energy efficiency improvement of universities and other higher education facilities in Ukraine. - New initiatives directed on a continuation of efforts in municipal services, mainly related to improved energy efficiency in district heating and in public buildings, as well as initiatives to expand the focus of energy efficiency improvement.
- Program for further support of district heating in Ukraine, as a continuation of the efforts initiated with the DemoUkrainaDH programme. - A sector study for opportunities for integrated agricultural and bioenergy projects to support Waste-to-Energy in Ukraine based on NEFCOs work with agricultural open burning problems within the context of the Barents and Arctic programmes in the region.
Additional resources placed in the fund for technical assistance will enable NEFCO to finance fees, travel and other reimbursable costs of consultancy companies, engaged by NEFCO in Ukraine, secondment of staff to NEFCO, for the development, implementation, monitoring and supervision of potential NEFCO projects and programmes or other such projects and programmes of Swedish interest in Ukraine. Typical assignments to be financed from the resources of the fund include: scoping missions, feasibility studies, project implementation support etc.

description.narrative:
During 2024, Sida has approved the following allocations to projects from the Fund (in SEK):
Lutsk Flue Gas Condenser PIU Support Consultant assignment (1,000,000) Horishni Plavni DH Extension of PIU Support Consultant assignment (600,000) IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute - Vinnytsia Modelling-based identification of district heating investment projects in Vinnytsia (750,000) Kremenchuk DH Rakivka project PIU Support Consultant assignment (2,250,000)
Cumulatively, the fund has since 2009 been supporting 78 assignments. Most of them have been related to different investment programmes and initiatives in municipal environment infrastructure, many, but not all, with Swedish co-financing. Below are the most important ones:
The DemoUkrainaDH programme, with investment grant financing from the Sida-Nefco DemoUkrainaDH Investment Co-financing Fund was implemented in the period 2011-2022. Demonstration projects in tweleve cities were successfully implemented.
Sweden-Ukraine District Heating (SUDH) Fund, four full-size DH projects supported with Swedish co-financing.
Ukraine Higher Education (UHE) project with energy efficiency projects in five universities.
The NIP-Nefco Ukraine Water Modernisation Programme, with the objective to implement 10-13 water and/or wastewater projects.
Nordic Energy Efficiency and Humanitarian Support Initiative (NIU), established in the fall of 2014 providing grant funds to projects in five regions of South-East Ukraine.
Norway-Ukraine Energy Efficiency Initiative (NUEE), three projects.
Eastern Europe Energy Efficiency and Environment Partnership (E5P), about twenty projects so far.
EU-funded investment programmes, e.g. EU support for urgent housing for IDP in Ukraine
Cumulatively, completed projects so far has, inter alias, led to reductions in CO2 emissions with more than 50 000 tonnes per year. Important to note though that the fund only finances technical assistance related to those projects. The programmes and initiatives above are financing or co-financing the investment parts.
